what_its_for: Methenamine mandelate is an antibiotic used to prevent or treat recurring urinary tract infections (UTIs). It works by releasing a substance in your urine that kills the bacteria causing the infection. It is most often used as a long-term preventive treatment, not for active severe infections.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. You may take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush or chew the tablets — swallow them whole. Take every dose exactly as your doctor prescribed, even if you feel fine. Drink plenty of fluids throughout the day unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 gram (1000 mg) taken 4 times a day, after meals and at bedtime. For children 6 to 12 years old, the typical dose is 500 mg taken 4 times a day. For children under 6, the dose is based on body weight and will be determined by the doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids while on this medicine, as they can make it less effective by reducing the acidity of your urine. Avoid foods and drinks that make your urine less acidic (alkaline), such as large amounts of citrus juices, milk, or baking soda products, unless your doctor approves. Do not share this medication with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a skin rash, hives, or itching; severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; painful or difficult urination; blood in your urine; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; or if your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse after a few days of treatment. Also call your doctor if you develop a fever, chills, or back or side pain, which could mean the infection has spread to your kidneys.
when_it_works: This medicine may take several days to start reducing symptoms. For prevention of UTIs, it works best when taken consistently every day as prescribed. You may not notice immediate changes, especially if you are taking it to prevent infection. Finish the full course of treatment even if you feel better.
special_populations: Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally not recommended near the end of pregnancy. Breastfeeding: Small amounts may pass into breast milk; consult your doctor before use. Elderly patients: Use with caution and follow your doctor's dosing instructions carefully. Children under 6: Dosing must be carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's weight.
